title: The manifest of a tower-upgrade run

blocks.text: A telecom operator plans tower upgrades with a nightly MILP. Each run leaves a record like

The operator's harness compares runs by their manifest bytes. Write `manifest_bytes(record)` that returns those bytes: everything a rerun of the same inputs on the same software must reproduce, in one canonical JSON form, and nothing that a rerun need not reproduce or that names the machine.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from tower_manifest import manifest_bytes

record = {"inputs_digest": "a17b03", "solver": "highs", "params": {"random_seed": 5},
          "versions": {"ortools": "9.0"}, "status": "OPTIMAL", "objective": 455.0,
          "plan": {"TX-3": 2031, "TX-1": 2030},
          "started_at": "2030-01-05T03:10:00", "wall_seconds": 12.9, "host": "node-a"}

print("manifest:", manifest_bytes(record))
print("same run, other clock and host:",
      manifest_bytes({**record, "started_at": "2030-01-06T03:11:00", "wall_seconds": 13.4, "host": "node-b"})
      == manifest_bytes(record))
print("same run, objective 450:", manifest_bytes({**record, "objective": 450.0}) == manifest_bytes(record))

cases.says: the bytes hold the inputs, solver, versions and result, and a different objective gives different bytes
start time and wall time are left out
the host name is left out
the same plan stored in another order gives the same bytes

origin.section: A Run Manifest Records What Went In and What Came Out, and Leaves Out the Clock

concepts: a manifest keeps what a rerun must reproduce and leaves out the clock and the machine
